[Cultivars](/wiki/Cultivar "Cultivar") of *Hippeastrum* are popular indoor [ornamental plants](/wiki/Ornamental_plants "Ornamental plants") prized for their large brightly colored flowers (including red, pink, salmon, orange and white). Montana is a large state with considerable variation in geography, topography and elevation, and the climate is equally varied. The state spans from below the [45th parallel](/wiki/45th_parallel_north "45th parallel north") (the line equidistant between the equator and [North Pole](/wiki/North_Pole "North Pole")) to the [49th parallel](/wiki/49th_parallel_north "49th parallel north"), and elevations range from under 2,000 feet (610 m) to nearly 13,000 feet (4,000 m) above sea level. The western half is mountainous, interrupted by numerous large valleys. [Eastern Montana](/wiki/Eastern_Montana "Eastern Montana") comprises plains and badlands, broken by hills and isolated mountain ranges, and has a [semi-arid](/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate"), [continental](/wiki/Continentality "Continentality") climate ([Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *[BSk](/wiki/Cold_steppe "Cold steppe")*). The [Continental Divide](/wiki/Continental_Divide "Continental Divide") has a considerable effect on the climate, as it restricts the flow of warmer air from the Pacific from moving east, and drier continental air from moving west. The average distance between Saturn and the Sun is over 1.4 billion kilometers (9 [AU](/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit")). With an average orbital speed of 9.68 km/s,[[6]](#cite_note-fact-7) it takes Saturn 10,759 Earth days (or about 29+1⁄2 years)[[94]](#cite_note-cain2009-96) to finish one revolution around the Sun.[[6]](#cite_note-fact-7) As a consequence, it forms a near 5:2 [mean-motion resonance](/wiki/Mean-motion_resonance "Mean-motion resonance") with Jupiter.[[95]](#cite_note-97) The elliptical orbit of Saturn is inclined 2.48° relative to the [orbital plane](/wiki/Orbital_plane "Orbital plane") of the Earth.[[6]](#cite_note-fact-7) The [perihelion and aphelion](/wiki/Apsis "Apsis") distances are, respectively, 9.195 and 9.957 AU, on average.[[6]](#cite_note-fact-7)[[96]](#cite_note-98)

Saturn only has one known [trojan asteroid](/wiki/Trojan_asteroid "Trojan asteroid"), designated [2019 UO14](/wiki/2019_UO14 "2019 UO14"), whose trojan configuration was announced in September 2024, orbiting the Sun at the stable [L4](/wiki/Lagrange_point#L4_and_L5 "Lagrange point") [Lagrange point](/wiki/Lagrange_point "Lagrange point") 60° ahead of the planet along its orbit.[[97]](#cite_note-Hui2024-99) This discovery leaves only Mercury without any known trojans at all. Star Wars :: Cultural impact :: Industry :: chunk_0034
The original *Star Wars* film was a huge success for [20th Century Fox](/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"), and was credited for reinvigorating the company. Within three weeks of the film's release, the studio's stock price doubled to a record high. Prior to 1977, 20th Century Fox's greatest annual profits were $37 million, while in 1977, the company broke that record by posting a profit of $79 million.[[279]](#cite_note-EmpireOfDreams-285) The franchise helped Fox to change from an almost bankrupt [production company](/wiki/Production_company "Production company") to a thriving media conglomerate.[[301]](#cite_note-Cook-308) With over $10.3 billion in worldwide box office receipts, *Star Wars* is the [second-highest-grossing film franchise](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films#Highest-grossing_franchises_and_film_series "List of highest-grossing films") of all time.[[302]](#cite_note-:0-309)[[303]](#cite_note-:1-310)

*Star Wars* fundamentally changed the aesthetics and narratives of [Hollywood](/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") films, switching the focus of Hollywood-made films from deep, meaningful stories based on dramatic conflict, themes and [irony](/wiki/Irony "Irony"), to sprawling special-effects-laden [blockbusters](/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)"), as well as changing the Hollywood film industry in fundamental ways. Before *Star Wars*, special effects in films had not appreciably advanced since the 1950s.[[304]](#cite_note-Bigsby-311) The commercial success of *Star Wars* created a boom in state-of-the-art special effects in the late 1970s.[[301]](#cite_note-Cook-308) Along with *[Jaws](/wiki/Jaws_(film) "Jaws (film)")*, *Star Wars* started the tradition of the summer blockbuster film in the entertainment industry, where films open on many screens at the same time and profitable [franchises](/wiki/Media_franchise "Media franchise")

Ruth Simmons :: Career :: Prairie View A&M University presidency :: chunk_0006
In 2017, after five years of retirement, Simmons accepted an offer to serve as the interim president of [Prairie View A&M University](/wiki/Prairie_View_A%26M_University "Prairie View A&M University"), an [HBCU](/wiki/Historically_black_colleges_and_universities "Historically black colleges and universities") in her home state of [Texas](/wiki/Texas "Texas"). She served as interim president from July 1, 2017 to December 3, 2017.[[42]](#cite_note-42) On December 4, 2017, she was selected as the eighth president of Prairie View A&M University, becoming the first woman to do so.[[43]](#cite_note-43)[[44]](#cite_note-44)

At Prairie View A&M, Simmons focused her efforts on improving the university's financial stability, particularly on fundraising through an anonymous donor for the *Panther Success Grants* for undergraduates. Her vision for the university was to "ensure that Prairie View A&M University sustains excellence in teaching, research, and service for another 140-plus years...we will raise funds in a new and vital way so that the University will have the flexibility it needs to advance and make more visible its reach."[[9]](#cite_note-bloomberg_revives-a-black-college-9)[[45]](#cite_note-45) On March 11, 2022, Simmons announced that she would retire from her role as president when the university named her successor.[[2]](#cite_note-diverseeducation.com-2)

In 2022, Prairie View A&M announced that scholarships had increased and donations to the university had grown by 40% during Simmons’ 5-year presidency.[[4]](#cite_note-McGee-4)
